**Aspose.PDF FOSS for C++ 26.11** is a free, open-source, MIT-licensed C++20 library for working
with PDF documents. It can open, render, edit, and create PDFs, and it links against nothing but
the C++ standard library. Every codec and the page rasteriser are implemented from scratch. The
public API is a strict subset of Aspose.PDF for .NET, so class and method names will be familiar
to anyone migrating from .NET.

## New version numbering

From this release on, the library uses the version notation that all Aspose products use:
**`YY.M`**, the year and month of the release. 26.11 is the November 2026 release, the one after it
in December will be 26.12, and January 2027 will be 27.1. A fix released between monthly releases
adds a third number, for example 26.11.1. The jump from 1.0.1 to 26.11 is only this renumbering;
there were no releases in between.

What this means in practice:

- **Git tags** are `v26.11`, `v26.12`, and so on.
- **NuGet** always shows three numbers, so 26.11 appears there as `26.11.0`. NuGet sorts it after
  1.0.1, so *Update* in Visual Studio moves existing projects to it.
- **CMake:** the package version is `26.11`. `find_package(aspose_pdf_foss 26.11)` accepts any
  later release of the same year (26.12 and so on). A version request with an older major
  number, such as the `1.0` used with earlier releases, no longer matches: update it to `26.11`.

## What's new in 26.11

The full list is in the changelog linked below. The main additions:

- **Gradients and styled generated content.** Axial and radial gradient fills
  (`GradientAxialShading`, `GradientRadialShading`) wherever a colour fills an area, a page
  background (`Page::Background`), and generated content that honours the styling the API
  already exposed: graph stroke, dash, fill and rounded corners, `ZIndex`, table, row and cell
  backgrounds, borders and text style, floating-box backgrounds and rounded borders.
- **Signing with your own certificate and verifying signatures.** `PdfFileSignature::Sign` and
  `Certify` sign with an RSA or ECDSA (P-256/384/521) key from a PKCS#12 file. `VerifySignature`,
  `VerifySigned` and `Signature::Verify` check the signed digest and the signature, and return
  false for a modified document. DocMDP certification, signature and usage-rights removal, and
  LTV detection are supported.
- **Forms.** `FormEditor` now really edits fields (attributes, appearance, limits, combs,
  alignment, renaming, list items, moving, copying from other PDFs, scripts and submit buttons).
  Field and annotation flattening work per field and per annotation. Fields can appear on
  several pages. Text-field appearances follow the field's font, size, alignment, multi-line and
  comb settings.
- **Facades.** Booklet and N-up layouts, margins and content resizing in `PdfFileEditor`;
  `PdfPageEditor::ApplyChanges` (rotation, zoom, page size, alignment, transitions);
  `PdfContentEditor` attachments, document actions, viewer preferences, image replacement and
  stamp editing; bookmark XML and HTML export and import; annotation import from XFDF, FDF and
  other PDFs.
- **Annotations.** Embedded video and audio (`RichMediaAnnotation`), printer marks, marked text
  of text-markup annotations, bold and italic FreeText ranges, and Line, Ink, Polygon, PolyLine,
  FreeText and FileAttachment annotations loaded from files.
- **Pages from other documents.** `PageCollection::Add` and `Insert` accept a page from another
  document and deep-import it.
- **Fax TIFF.** `TiffDevice` writes CCITT Group 3 and Group 4 TIFFs, and the TIFF reader decodes
  them.
- **Four new examples** (13–16): signing and verification, the Facades editors, embedded media,
  and fax TIFF output. Example 12 is redesigned as a ten-page brochure.

Many fixes make edits to loaded documents stick: changes to loaded annotations and form fields
are saved, other annotations on a page are no longer dropped when one is added, text inside Form
XObjects is extracted, documents with a nested page tree can be edited, and metadata can be set on
documents that have no `/Info` dictionary.

### Behaviour changes

- `Signature::Verify()` and `PdfFileSignature::VerifySignature` / `VerifySigned` now really
  verify. They used to report any signature covering the whole file as valid.
- Methods that are not implemented yet throw `std::logic_error` naming the missing capability,
  instead of silently doing nothing. `CheckboxField::Clone` is no longer `noexcept`.
- `PdfContentEditor` stamp indexes are 0-based, and `MoveStamp` / `MoveStampById` take the
  stamp's new lower-left corner.
- Saving an annotation type the library cannot write throws instead of dropping the annotation.

The full list of changes is in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/aspose-pdf-foss/Aspose.PDF-FOSS-for-Cpp/blob/v26.11/CHANGELOG.md).

## Downloads

| Asset | Platform | Toolchain | Contents |
|---|---|---|---|
| `aspose-pdf-foss-cpp-26.11-linux-x64-gcc13.tar.gz` | Linux x86-64 | GCC 13, libstdc++, built on Ubuntu 24.04 | `libaspose_pdf_foss.a` (Release, position-independent) |
| `aspose-pdf-foss-cpp-26.11-windows-x64-msvc.zip` | Windows x64 | MSVC (Visual Studio 2022), dynamic CRT | `aspose_pdf_foss.lib` (Release, `/MD`) and `aspose_pdf_fossd.lib` (Debug, `/MDd`) |
| `Aspose.PDF.Cpp.FOSS.26.11.0.nupkg` | Windows x64, x86, ARM64 | Visual Studio 2022+ (MSBuild) | The signed NuGet package, also published on [nuget.org](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspose.PDF.Cpp.FOSS) |
| `SHA256SUMS.txt` | — | — | SHA-256 checksums of the assets |
| Source code (zip / tar.gz) | any | any C++20 compiler | Full source tree, generated by GitHub |

Every archive contains:

- `include/`: the public headers, including the single-entry header `aspose.pdf.foss.hpp`.
- `lib/`: the static library and the CMake package files (`lib/cmake/aspose_pdf_foss/`).
- `share/doc/aspose_pdf_foss/`: `LICENSE`, `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`, and the OFL 1.1 text for the
  bundled fonts.
- `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, and `BUILDINFO.txt` (exact compiler and commit used for the
  build).

Each archive was built, tested, and then compiled and run as a `find_package` consumer before it
was attached to this release. To verify a download:
`sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS.txt --ignore-missing`.

## Getting started

### Visual Studio (NuGet)

Install [`Aspose.PDF.Cpp.FOSS`](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspose.PDF.Cpp.FOSS) through
**Manage NuGet Packages**, or from the Package Manager Console:

```powershell
Install-Package Aspose.PDF.Cpp.FOSS
```

The package adds the include path, links the library that matches your platform (x64, Win32, or
ARM64) and configuration, and raises the project to C++20. Your code only needs
`#include <aspose.pdf.foss.hpp>`.

### From a release archive (CMake)

Extract the archive, then point CMake at it:

```cmake
find_package(aspose_pdf_foss 26.11 CONFIG REQUIRED)
target_link_libraries(your_app PRIVATE aspose_pdf_foss::aspose_pdf_foss)
```

```bash
cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/path/to/aspose-pdf-foss-cpp-26.11-linux-x64-gcc13
```

The imported target switches your target to C++20 automatically. On Windows, CMake selects the
Release or Debug library to match your configuration.

### From source (CMake subdirectory)

```cmake
add_subdirectory(Aspose.PDF-FOSS-for-Cpp)
target_link_libraries(your_app PRIVATE aspose_pdf_foss::aspose_pdf_foss)
```

Building from source needs CMake 3.20+, a C++20 compiler (GCC 13+, Clang 16+, or MSVC 2022 17.5+),
and Python 3 at build time only.

### Hello, PDF

```cpp
#include <aspose.pdf.foss.hpp>
#include <fstream>
#include <iostream>

int main() {
    Aspose::Pdf::Document doc("input.pdf");
    std::cout << "Pages: " << doc.Pages().Count() << "\n";

    Aspose::Pdf::Text::TextAbsorber absorber;
    absorber.Visit(doc);
    std::cout << absorber.Text() << "\n";

    Aspose::Pdf::Devices::PngDevice png(Aspose::Pdf::Devices::Resolution(150));
    std::ofstream out("page1.png", std::ios::binary);
    png.Process(doc.Pages()[1], out);
}
```

The [`examples/`](https://github.com/aspose-pdf-foss/Aspose.PDF-FOSS-for-Cpp/tree/v26.11/examples)
directory has 16 runnable programs, including a ten-page from-scratch brochure.

## Compatibility

- **Language:** C++20. The public headers use C++20 standard-library features such as `std::span`.
- **Prebuilt Linux library:** link with GCC 13 or newer, or with Clang against libstdc++ 13 or
  newer, on a system with glibc 2.39 or newer (Ubuntu 24.04 or later). For other distributions or
  toolchains, build from source.
- **Prebuilt Windows libraries (zip and NuGet):** link with the same or a newer MSVC toolset,
  using the dynamic CRT (`/MD` for Release, `/MDd` for Debug). This is the CMake and Visual Studio
  default. Debug libraries carry embedded debug info, so no separate PDB is needed.
- **Runtime dependencies:** none.

## Known limitations

- The `XmpValue` helpers `IsDateTime`, `IsField`, `IsNamedValue`, `IsRaw`, `IsNamedValues`, and
  `IsStructure` always return `false`; dates and structures read from a file come back as
  strings. Use `IsString`, `IsInteger`, `IsDouble`, and `IsArray` instead.
- Signature verification checks the signed digest and the signature against the embedded
  certificate. It does not validate the certificate's trust chain or revocation status.
- Standard-14 fallback fonts cover Helvetica, Times-Roman, and Courier (four styles each). Symbol
  and ZapfDingbats have no bundled fallback.
- A few methods are not implemented yet and throw `std::logic_error` naming the missing
  capability.
- Objects added to `Paragraphs`, `Annotations`, `Form`, `Artifacts`, and `Outlines` are stored by
  reference, so they must outlive `Save()`.
- Encryption permissions are enforced by PDF viewers; the library is not a DRM mechanism.

[Aspose.PDF for C++ Enterprise Edition](https://products.aspose.com/pdf/cpp/) does not have these
limitations and covers a broader feature set.
